newsitem.title: USA: Fund managers neutral on US debt durations--survey.
newsitem.headline: Fund managers neutral on US debt durations--survey.

text.p: Money managers were neutral on duration in U.S. portfolio structures over the past week, following three weeks of extending duration, according to a survey by Stone & McCarthy Research Associates.
"Money managers have generally moved steadily closer to neutral after being short to an extent that approached historically extreme measures as recently as four weeks ago," the report said.

"There had recently been a modest divergence between the survey average and asset-weighted duration statistics, as average measures of duration exposure increased significantly, while asset-weighted measures of duration exposure were steady," it said.
Duration refers to a portfolio's average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
In the week ended May 27, the cash/assets ratio rose to 9.14 percent from 8.90 percent on an arithmetic basis but fell to 6.21 percent from 6.52 percent on a weighted basis.
The survey's actual/target duration index declined to 98.97 percent from 99.25 percent on an arithmetic basis and rose to 98.99 percent from 98.00 percent on a weighted basis.
The survey's bear/bull index held steady at 4.78 on an arithmetic basis. It held firm at 4.71 on an asset-weighted basis.
A number above 5.00 is seen as indicating investors are mostly long on the market.
None of the portfolio managers surveyed said they were planning to be active in the coming week, down from nine percent the week before.
The Stone & McCarthy survey is conducted by the research firm weekly. It includes 25 market participants with total assets of about $100 billion, the firm said.
* Table provided by Stone and McCarthy Research Associates.
** Respondents intending to adjust portfolio in coming week.
